correctness.rationale: On one n-world universal S5 class with r Boolean set inputs (m=2^r atom types), induction on term structure shows truth at a world depends on local atom type and counts clipped at K; the identity min(K,sum c_i)=min(K,sum min(K,c_i)) controls nested counting. Conversely, any realizable clipped histogram has a depth-one characteristic test, so every assignment of output bits to supported local types is definable. Counting supports over admissible vectors yields E and the generating function. Clipping is injective on exact compositions iff n<=2K, giving the sharp full permutation-equivariant grade K=ceil(n/2); for n>=mK every saturated clipped histogram is realized, giving the stable exponent and sharp missing all-K profile at n=mK-1. Independent exact enumeration compared all 198 chosen finite (n,m,K) cases with closed exponents and thresholds; no finite list substitutes for the induction and construction.

value.rationale: Counting all term operations (rather than formula equivalence at a pointed input) is a natural exact finite-algebraic invariant. The theorem gives a functional-completeness classification, an explicit exact operation census and two sharp minimal thresholds for expressive grade and size stabilization. It supplies a reusable complete description of bounded counting logic over a single finite S5 cluster rather than merely a textbook ungraded depth collapse.
